hero.title: A visual walkthrough of the QR ordering platform for modern cafes.
hero.description: CafeQR brings the guest menu, cashier counter, kitchen handoff, cafe administration, and SaaS operations into one App Router product. This guide explains the platform at a practical level for potential clients, partners, and technical reviewers.

overview.title: One product surface for guests, staff, owners, and operators
paragraphs: CafeQR is designed for cafes that want a polished digital ordering flow without slowing down service. Guests order from a QR menu, cashiers approve and manage tickets, kitchen staff receive printed receipts, and cafe owners control menu content from an admin console.

Under the hood, every cafe is treated as a tenant. A tenant slug connects the public QR menu, cashier terminal, kitchen printing setup, admin console, products, orders, tables, and subscription status.
overview.calloutBody: Fast enough for daily service, elegant enough for premium hospitality, and structured enough to grow into a serious SaaS business.

coreSuite.title: Five coordinated tools instead of isolated screens

qr.title: QR Menu
qr.body: Guests scan a table-specific route, browse the active menu, manage a cart, and submit orders without installing an app.

pos.title: POS Cashier
pos.body: Cashiers approve QR orders, create walk-in tickets, manage statuses, and keep the counter moving from one focused terminal.

kitchen.title: Kitchen Receipt Printing
kitchen.body: Accepted orders flow to the kitchen printer so staff receive confirmed tickets with table, items, quantities, notes, and time.

admin.title: Admin Console
admin.body: Cafe owners maintain products, multilingual menu details, QR tables, staff PINs, settings, and sales views from a private surface.

saas.title: SaaS Control Panel
saas.body: The operator layer provisions cafes, manages plan status, reviews receipts, and keeps tenant operations organized centrally.

architecture.title: Multi-tenant routing with realtime operations
architecture.paragraph: The production app uses Next.js App Router routes to separate guest, cashier, kitchen, admin, demo, and onboarding experiences. Tenant-specific routes read the cafe slug, validate the requested surface, and keep order data attached to the correct cafe.

routing.title: Tenant routing
routing.body: Cafe-facing surfaces live under dynamic cafe routes, while demo and onboarding pages stay separate.

isolation.title: Supabase isolation
isolation.body: Cafe records, products, tables, orders, receipts, owners, and subscription state are keyed by tenant data.

realtime.title: Realtime order sync
realtime.body: Guest orders appear at the POS quickly, then move through approval, printing, ready, and completed states.

actions.title: Server actions
actions.body: Sensitive mutations are handled through server-side actions with validation before business data changes.

security.title: Layered controls around tenants, roles, sessions, and subscriptions
security.paragraph: CafeQR uses a practical security posture for a hospitality SaaS: validate the tenant before exposing a surface, limit role access, keep sensitive credentials outside source control, and enforce subscription state where ordering operations happen.

headers.title: HTTP hardening
headers.body: Middleware adds defensive headers and issues an HTTP-only session fingerprint cookie.

owner.title: Owner authorization
owner.body: Cafe admin access is tied to authenticated owner identity and cafe ownership checks.

pin.title: Staff PIN gates
pin.body: Cashier and kitchen entry can be protected by staff PIN controls and terminal limits.

subscription.title: Subscription enforcement
subscription.body: Expired or suspended cafes can be blocked from guest ordering and operational surfaces.

security.calloutBody: This public-facing documentation intentionally describes the architecture without exposing service-role keys, private operator paths, production credentials, or database secrets.

business.title: A lightweight setup for small and medium-sized cafes
business.paragraph: The product is built around hardware that cafe teams already understand: a browser-based POS, optional customer receipt printing, one kitchen thermal printer, QR codes on tables, and standard guest phones.

printer.title: Kitchen printer
printer.body: An ESC/POS-compatible thermal printer is recommended for automatic kitchen tickets after cashier approval.

pos.title: POS terminal
pos.body: A Windows PC, laptop, tablet, or touchscreen device running a modern browser can operate the cashier surface.

admin.title: Admin device
admin.body: A laptop or tablet gives owners the best management experience, with responsive support for quick mobile updates.

internet.title: Reliable internet
internet.body: Realtime ordering, authentication, and tenant data all depend on a stable connection during service.

guests.title: Guest phones
guests.body: Guests only need a modern smartphone camera and browser to scan, browse, and order.

stack.title: Modern web tooling tuned for realtime service
rows: Framer Motion, realtime audio cues, lucide-react
Standalone Next.js, PM2, Caddy-ready VPS profile

structure.title: A route-first App Router layout
structure.paragraph: The codebase is organized around product surfaces, server actions, shared utilities, landing components, and demo state. The overview below keeps private operational details out while showing how the public product is composed.
structure.code:
CafeQrSaaS/
|-- middleware.ts
|-- next.config.ts
|-- src/
|   |-- actions/
|   |   |-- auth.ts        owner auth, PIN checks, menu and order actions
|   |   |-- saas.ts        subscription and tenant operations
|   |-- app/
|   |   |-- page.tsx       landing page
|   |   |-- tutorial/      product guide
|   |   |-- demo/          local interactive demo surfaces
|   |   |-- [cafeSlug]/    tenant guest, cashier, and admin routes
|   |-- components/
|   |   |-- landing/       public marketing and demo components
|   |-- lib/

|       |-- demoStore.ts   shared demo products and orders
|       |-- utils.ts       Tailwind class merge helper

guestFlow.title: From table scan to kitchen ticket
guestFlow.paragraph: The guest journey is intentionally short. A QR scan opens the right cafe and table, the app validates that ordering is available, then the customer sends a pending order to the POS for staff approval.
steps: Loads the cafe menu and cart.

posFlow.title: Cashier approval keeps the kitchen clean
posFlow.paragraph: The POS is the operational hub. Cashiers unlock the terminal, receive pending QR orders, accept or reject them, create walk-in orders, trigger kitchen receipts, and move tickets through ready and completed states.
lines: checks active tenant and device limits
receives pending guest orders in realtime
accepts, rejects, or creates walk-in order
marks order ready, paid, and completed

saasFlow.title: Provision once, operate many cafes
saasFlow.paragraph: The SaaS layer turns the product from a single-cafe app into a managed platform. Operators provision a cafe, connect an owner, configure plan limits, then allow each cafe team to operate inside its own tenant boundary.
steps: Creates plan, slug, owner, and limits.
Manages menu, QR tables, and staff access.

liveDemo.title: Explore each product surface
liveDemo.paragraph: The demo routes use a browser-local synchronized store, which means reviewers can test the end-to-end experience without production tenant credentials.

roadmap.title: Where the platform can grow next
items: Advanced analytics for peak hours, revenue patterns, and product performance.
AI-assisted menu descriptions and demand forecasting.
Custom domain onboarding for premium tenants.
Expanded billing automation and receipt review workflows.
